title: Nigerian Goat Pepper Soup with Scent Leaf
summary: A fiery, aromatic Nigerian broth of bone-in goat simmered with a home-toasted pepper-soup spice, ginger and Scotch bonnet, finished with scent leaf and sliced red chilli.
equipment: spice grinder or pestle and mortar

ingredients.item: bone-in goat meat, in 4-5 cm chunks
Scotch bonnet chilli, pierced (or chopped for more heat)
fine sea salt or table salt
scent leaf (efirin) or Thai basil leaves

steps.title: Grind the spice
steps.text: Toast the coriander, cumin, fennel, peppercorns and cloves in the dry pan over medium heat for 1-2 min until fragrant. Cool, grind to a powder and stir in the nutmeg.

steps.title: Season the goat
steps.text: Rinse the goat, drain and put it in the pot with the onion, ginger, garlic, Scotch bonnet, chilli flakes, half the salt and half the spice mix. Stir well and leave 15 min.

steps.title: Steam in its juices
steps.text: Set the pot over medium heat, cover and cook 10 min, stirring once or twice, so the meat releases its juices and absorbs the spice.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in the water, bring to the boil, skim, then cover and simmer gently for 1½-2 h until the goat is tender and pulls from the bone.

steps.title: Spice the broth
steps.text: Stir in the rest of the spice and salt and simmer 10 min more, uncovered, so the broth darkens and tastes peppery. Taste and add a little hot water if it is too strong.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the torn scent leaf and fish out the Scotch bonnet if you prefer it milder.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into bowls with plenty of broth and scatter over the sliced red chilli. Serve as it is, or with boiled yam or white rice.

tips: Steaming the goat in its own juices before adding water gives a deeper-flavoured broth.
Add the second half of the spice near the end so the broth stays peppery and fragrant.
Thai basil is the closest easy swap for scent leaf (efirin).
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until boiling and add fresh leaves to serve. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
